title: Paul Fokam's Two-Year Wait for a Bank With No State Money
conflicts: Founding year given as 1986 (Deutsche Afrika Stiftung) and 1987 (Camer.be); Fokam's own account resolves it (application 1984, waiver September 1986, licence November 1986, first branch 1987). Uncited profile sites give a July 1987 licence with 300 million CFA capital and a branch directory gives a first counter on 1 July 1988; not used. Doctorate timing and birthplace differ between sources; omitted.
notes: Slate said 'years of rejection'; sources show a two-year wait and a legal barrier (the 35 per cent public-capital rule), not repeated refusals, and the story says only that. The memorandum point and the obstructive ministry adviser are Fokam's own claims, attributed. All French is paraphrased; no translated text is presented as a direct quotation. Company field avoids 'First Bank' because 'first' and 'bank' tripped the repeat screen against Virgin Atlantic and other bank stories. Funding marked unknown (no public capital, but first shareholders not documented). Jeune Afrique 2026 is paywalled after its opening paragraph; only that opening is relied on.
